about: What Pari Pakuru' (1979) says of its own two dialects: the contents page and the chapter 'The Pawnee Alphabet' (pp. xviii-xxiv of the book, pages 20-26 of the scan). Read from the scan on 2026-11-15, each line cut out and read once by the session that made this file; the lessons' reading of 2026-11-14 did not cover the front matter. English is quoted as printed. Pawnee words are as printed; in a pronunciation (the spellings in parentheses) the book underlines a long vowel, written here with a low line after the vowel (a̲). 'Skidi' is the book's spelling of Skiri. The file holds statements and the book's own examples, nothing worked out from them.

statements.about: a lesson title printed in both dialects
statements.text: 3 KIRIKÉ RUT•U'? (SB) / KÍRIKU RUT•U'? (SK) / What Does It Look Like?
Some vowels, however, will vary in length and quality depending on who is speaking and what dialect is being used.

statements.about: the letter e in the alphabet table: South Band as in 'pet', Skidi as in 'pit'
statements.text: e (e) pet (SB) akse cow / pit (SK) (ák-si) cow

statements.about: long e: South Band as in 'fiancé', Skidi as in 'receipt'
h at the beginning of a word is silent for South Band speakers
r is silent after h for Skidi speakers
hr is said h by Skidi speakers
statements.text: The combination hr is a breathy version of r which is pronounced simply as h by Skidi speakers, so that the r is silent.

statements.about: South Band speakers do not say h at the beginning of a word
statements.text: Silent h: South Band speakers do not pronounce h at the beginning of words; the h will be silent as in English honor.

statements.about: the vowel written e is South Band; Skidi speakers say i
statements.text: There are four main vowels in Pawnee, though the South Band e is pronounced by Skidi speakers just as if it were an i.
statements.note: A flaw in the scan lies over the two words 'if it'; the rest of the line leaves no doubt of them.

statements.about: South Band speakers have more long vowels; the learner chooses a dialect
statements.text: You will find that South Band speakers have more long vowels than do Skidi speakers, so you should decide which dialect you will concentrate on, and mark your textbook for the particular sounds of that dialect.

statements.about: two vowels together: South Band speakers break between them, Skidi speakers glide
statements.text: This is especially true for South Band speakers. Skidi speakers are more likely to glide two vowels together. […] Notice the Skidi pronunciation sounds like English cow.

statements.about: the accent marks of the book are South Band
statements.text: IMPORTANT. The accent marked in this book is that of some South Band speakers. There will be other speakers who use a slightly different accent.
